newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Regent says won't invest in local Gazprom stock.
newsitem.headline: Regent says won't invest in local Gazprom stock.

text.p: Regent Gaz Investment Co Ltd, which was proposing to set up a foreign-traded fund investing in domestic shares of Russian gas monopoly Gazprom, said it would not invest in local Gazprom shares.

"The Board has taken this decision with regret as we continue to believe that our strategy to help passive investors participate in RAO Gazprom's success was appropriate and legal," it said in a draft press release from Regent Fund Management, dated February 21 and received by Reuters on Monday.

Regent Pacific Group, the parent of Regent European Securities which is operating in Moscow, "remains committed to investing in Russia and maintaining its close links and good relations with the local business community," it said.
A letter explaining how shareholders in the new fund could redeem shares will be sent out this week, it said.

Hong Kong-based Regent Fund Management, part of the Regent Pacific Group, is manager of the Regent Gaz Investment Company Limited. Regent European Securities, a Moscow broker, is also a group subsidiary.
Gazprom said last Monday it had written to Regent Fund requiring it to stop the off-shore fund that intended to invest in domestic Gazprom shares.

"RAO Gazprom intends to take all necessary steps to prevent the realisation of Regent Fund's plan and other similar schemes regarding the shares of the Company," Gazprom said of the plan by Regent Gaz Investment Company Limited.
Gazprom said it believed the proposed Regent fund was contrary to "normative acts of the Russian Federation providing for national security" and Gazprom's charter.

Gazprom did not specify what steps it would take to stop Regent Gaz, based in the Cayman Islands. Gazprom had said Regent intended to create a $200 million fund backed by domestic Gazprom shares bought by a Regent subsidiary in Russia.
Regent said it had received advice that its proposed investment was lawful.

"However, in view of the stated position of RAO Gazprom, the Directors and the Company's Manager have concluded that it would be inadvisable now to seek to invest the Company's assets in RAO Gazprom shares," it said.
Gazprom in October 1996 launched an American Depositary Share (ADS) which allows international trading in Gazprom but trades at a price about four times that of underlying shares traded in Russia.

The premium is based largely on the difficulty of buying and trading local shares in the world's largest natural gas company and a number of equity analysts and traders have said the price of Gazprom's ADSs would be hurt by the plan.
Gazprom shares in Moscow closed on Friday unchanged from Thursday's close at $0.512. They had not been traded by 0845 GMT on Monday.
Gazprom ADSs in London were trading at 0845 GMT at $20.675, up from $20.005 at Friday's close.
